definition: The Transformer model is a type of architecture that relies solely on attention mechanisms to draw global dependencies between input and output.
details: The Transformer model is a type of architecture that relies solely on attention mechanisms to draw global dependencies between input and output. The Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) is a version of Transformer with a specific training method that uses unsupervised learning, which then can be fine-tuned with supervised learning tasks.

explainer.lead: The Transformer relies solely on attention mechanisms to draw global dependencies between input and output; GPT is a Transformer version trained unsupervised and then fine-tunable with supervised tasks. This training recipe is why pretrained language models can be adapted to many downstream tasks.

tiers.eli5: The model pays attention to all parts of the input at once, and GPT first learns from lots of raw text on its own before being taught specific tasks.
tiers.practitioner: You pretrain the Transformer with unsupervised learning on raw text, then fine-tune with supervised tasks. The pitfall is that the fine-tuning stage shapes performance heavily, so pretraining alone is not the finished system.
tiers.paperLevel: The Transformer draws global dependencies between input and output using only attention mechanisms. GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) adds a specific training method using unsupervised learning, which can then be fine-tuned with supervised learning tasks.

explainer.example: A GPT model is pretrained unsupervised on a large text corpus, then fine-tuned with supervised examples for a specific task.
